owner: Executive director, until the board names an owner
why: We want AI to give providers their evenings back. We must protect patients and keep care safe.
who_it_covers: Staff, volunteers, contractors and board members, at both locations.

tools.name: EHR AI scribe
tools.approved_for: Three-provider pilot, business associate agreement signed. May hold patient information in those visits.

new_tools: Nadia (privacy and security officer) approves any new tool or AI feature that could touch patient information, after a business associate agreement. Beth (COO) approves others; clinical uses also need Dr. Okafor.
accounts: Use your work email. Turn off any vendor setting that trains on what you type.
everyone_now: Any AI tool, through your work email, for work with no information about a real person.
allowed_uses: Appointment reminder and sliding fee letter templates, with no patient details.
Patient education handouts, with no patient details.
Clinicians: general clinical lookups with no patient information.

needs_approval.use: Patient information in any tool beyond the scribe pilot

protected_information: Unless a tool above is approved for it: diagnoses, medications, behavioral health notes, HIV status and reproductive health (HIPAA). Substance use treatment records, with extra federal protection. Immigration status, sliding fee income documents, insurance numbers, staff files, the donor list, and all passwords.
off_limits: No tool that could touch patient information without a business associate agreement.
AI never makes a clinical decision or signs a note.
check_before_it_goes_out: A clinician reviews every word of AI notes and handouts before signing or sending. Check medications, names, numbers, tone.
A person checks billing and coding suggestions. Whoever sends it is responsible.
decisions_about_people: A person, not AI, decides sliding fee eligibility and who gets services. AI may help a clinician look things up.
being_open: Tell patients when the scribe is listening, and let them say no.
If we add a patient chatbot, it must say it is not a person.
if_something_goes_wrong: Tell Nadia right away. She runs the HIPAA breach clock.
Reporting a mistake is expected, never punished.
who_owns_this: The compliance committee reviews this policy; the board approves it.
open_questions: After the pilot, do we roll the scribe out to all providers, and should behavioral health use it?
Do we pay for or approve ChatGPT, OpenEvidence or UpToDate AI search for any use with patient information?
Who checks AI or Google Translate versions of Spanish patient materials?
What do we tell funders, like HRSA, who ask about AI?
